in_text_mentions: As she was not able to produce sputum, she under went videobronchoscopy. On bronchoscopy a large loose broncholith was seen at the opening of right middle lobe bronchus (Fig. III). Bronchial aspirate taken from both side of lung which was negative for acid fast bacilli and no organism was grown on culture. Smear prepared with the fragments failed to show any organism.

panels.body_site: right mainstem bronchus / station 4R mediastinal lymph node
panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial contrast-enhanced chest CT in lung window shows a densely calcified node/stone protruding into the right mainstem bronchus with airway narrowing, consistent with broncholithiasis. B: Axial contrast-enhanced chest CT in mediastinal window confirms a densely calcified station 4R node protruding into the right mainstem bronchus and narrowing the airway, consistent with broncholithiasis.
panels.attribution_text: Peñafiel-Pallares et al. Broncholithiasis: Diagnostic and Therapeutic Insights From a Contemporary Case Series of Five Patients.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.106167. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Computed tomography findings of broncholithiasis in Case 1. Axial contrast-enhanced chest CT images displayed in lung window (A) and mediastinal window (B) demonstrate calcified mediastinal lymphadenopathy with a large, densely calcified station 4R lymph node protruding into the right mainstem bronchus, resulting in significant airway narrowing (arrows). These findings are consistent with broncholithiasis secondary to prior granulomatous disease.
in_text_mentions: Ms. B, a 70-year-old female with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and a remote history of histoplasmosis, presented with two years of hemoptysis. Imaging revealed calcified mediastinal lymphadenopathy and a large, calcified station 4R lymph node protruding into the right mainstem bronchus (RMSB) (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial contrast-enhanced chest CT in lung window showing a calcified broncholith in the right lower lobe bronchus with complete obstruction in a 45-year-old patient with broncholithiasis. Associated post-obstructive changes are present, with extrinsic compression of the right middle lobe bronchus.

panels.rationale: Bronchoscopy image shows a pale calcified broncholith impacted within the bronchial lumen with surrounding erythematous, inflamed mucosa in a patient with broncholithiasis; caption and in-text mentions directly attribute the finding to broncholithiasis.

panels.figure_caption: Bronchoscopic findings in Case 2. Flexible bronchoscopy demonstrating a densely calcified broncholith causing complete (100%) obstruction of the superior segment of the left lower lobe (LLL). The surrounding bronchial mucosa appears erythematous and friable, consistent with chronic inflammation and bronchomalacia identified after balloon dilation.
in_text_mentions: Initial flexible bronchoscopy revealed 100% obstruction of the LLL superior segment (Figure 4). Balloon dilation with a controlled radial expansion (CRE) balloon (8-9-10 mm) was performed, revealing significant bronchomalacia and an underlying broncholith (Figure 4). Cultures grew Actinomyces and mixed molds, prompting ampicillin-sulbactam therapy followed by amoxicillin-clavulanate.

panels.rationale: H&E histopathology of an autopsy-recovered broncholith in a broncholithiasis case report, showing calcified core with concentric mineralized lamellar deposits; caption and in-text describe dystrophic calcification of a recovered biological structure, matching the broncholith histology finding.
panels.attribution_text: Zambiasi et al. Broncholithiasis mimicking metallic projectiles at autopsy: a forensic diagnostic pitfall in putrefied bodies.. International journal of legal medicine 2026. doi:10.1007/s00414-026-03916-9. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 5.
panels.figure_caption: Histological paraffin-embedded cross section (hematoxylin and eosin staining) of one of the recovered structures showing a calcified core surrounded by mineralized concentric lamellar deposits and decalcification artifacts in the outer part of the sample
in_text_mentions: Following a brief decalcification step, microscopic examination of one the recovered structures was performed to characterize their architecture. The sections revealed a calcified core surrounded by mineralized concentric lamellar deposits. No residual cellular structures or microorganisms were identified. Decalcification artifacts were present in the outer part of the sample (Fig. 5). These morphological features were indicative of dystrophic calcification of biological origin.

panels.rationale: Gross photograph of four puniceous/greyish stones recovered from the right upper lobe at autopsy, consistent with broncholiths; article title and caption identify broncholithiasis. Ruler markings provide scale (annotations present). Putrefied autopsy context and small size make this a variant gross presentation rather than the classic endobronchial or expectorated stone.

in_text_mentions: sions, indicating prior thoracic surgery or trauma. Diffuse aortic and coronary calcification were observed. The anterior interventricular artery and the abdominal aorta showed atherosclerotic plaques without significant stenosis or obstruction of the lumen. Macroscopic dissection of the right lung discovered four greyish elements with a stony consistency in the upper lobe, irregular, and spherical, ranging from 1 to 2 mm of diameter (Fig. 1). Due to advanced putrefactive changes, their precise anatomical location and distribution within the pulmonary parenchyma could not be reliably assessed.
